title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a computation. It is a short handwritten list of topics, almost certainly a syllabus or menu for a course, or a list of exposé or exam subjects. Grothendieck taught at Montpellier from the early 1970s, and the next page is a list of about ten student names, which supports this reading. The items are:
(1) Orientations: orientation of manifolds and orientation sheaves, as in Poincaré duality.
(2) Embeddings ('plongements', reading uncertain): embeddings of manifolds or surfaces.
(3) H^i and χ: (co)homology groups and the Euler–Poincaré characteristic.
(4) A bracketed block of three items on the fundamental group:
  - coverings ('revêtements') and π1;
  - the relation between π1 and Galois theory, i.e. the Galois correspondence between coverings and subgroups of π1, parallel to field extensions and subgroups of the Galois group;
  - coverings and functions of a complex variable, i.e. Riemann surfaces of algebraic functions and branched covers of P^1(C).
(5) The Weil conjectures, as a culminating topic linking topology (Betti numbers, Lefschetz fixed points) to counting points over finite fields.
The arc runs from elementary topology (orientation, homology, Euler characteristic) through coverings and their Galois-theoretic interpretation to the arithmetic payoff. This is the standard pedagogical skeleton behind Grothendieck's view of π1 and cohomology. The sheet was reused: the previous page is unrelated administrative typescript.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a teaching syllabus listing standard topics, from elementary topology through the Galois theory of coverings to the Weil conjectures. It is of mild historical interest only, as evidence of how Grothendieck structured his Montpellier teaching. There is no new mathematics on the page.
transcription_corrections: The second line is hard to read ('pl..gements'); 'plongements' is plausible but uncertain.
The third item in the bracketed block reads 'rev. et fonctions de var. complexes', where 'var. complexes' means variables complexes (complex variables).
